what: How far tracked off-plan projects are behind the first handover date we have on record, by market.

rules.quantile: linear interpolation between order statistics (type 7, as numpy and spreadsheet PERCENTILE.INC)
rules.current_handover: month of the currently published handover, from the best available record: the overdue watcher reading (today minus its months) when there is one; else the dated handover promise in /data/promises.json (moved to a later date when the same records show one); else the handover in the project research record in /data/named.json; the last month of the period named (a quarter counts as its third month, a year as December); else December of the advertised year in /data/bali-cases.json. on-time.json gives each project its source (hs) and the date the record was read (hr)
rules.past_current: not completed and the month now is after the current handover month (a watcher reading, or a dated record whose month has passed); a year-only date from /data/bali-cases.json that has passed without a reading stays inconsistent and is left out
rules.first_handover: current handover minus the recorded months the date has moved (delay)
rules.months_late: month now minus first handover, for projects not completed whose first handover has passed
rules.share_past_first: projects past the first handover / projects not completed with a usable handover date
rules.share_past_current: projects past the currently advertised handover / the same denominator

caveats: History starts in November 2026: one monthly snapshot is stored each month from now on, so trends need time.
Where only a year is public we assume December, and where no date move is recorded we assume none. Both can only understate lateness.
Dates are what developers and agents advertise, read from their pages. A misread date changes a project's figure.
The tracked projects are the ones being marketed now, not every project in a market. Projects that were finished and stopped marketing are under-represented.
